metadata.scenario: A prospect decides to cancel their scheduled service appointment, citing a change in needs. Category: Cancellation. Flags: cancellation_risk.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Rose Patterson. I wanted to talk about my mom's care services. Hi Rose! It's nice to hear from you. How's your mom doing? Well, that’s the thing. I need to cancel her companion care appointment for next week. I see. Can I ask what prompted the decision to cancel? Yes, we’ve had a change in our needs. My son is going to be around more and can help with her care. I understand, family support is very important. How is your mom adjusting to this change? She’s been okay, but I worry about her comfort with familiar caregivers. That's been key for her. Absolutely, continuity can really help with her comfort. Right, and I want to make sure we don’t lose that connection with her caregivers. Would you like to pause her services instead of canceling? We can keep her caregivers in the loop. That might be a good idea. What would that look like? We could schedule a follow-up call in a month to reassess her needs. Yes, I think that would be helpful. Great! I’ll set that up for you. And is there anything else we can assist with right now? Actually, I was wondering if we could still have someone come for extra support on days my son is busy? Absolutely, we can arrange for that. Would you like to keep the same caregivers? Yes, definitely. They know her well. Perfect, I’ll make a note of that. We can offer Companion Care on an as-needed basis. That sounds good. What's the rate for that? It's $25 to $30 per hour, depending on the specific needs during the visit. Okay, I’ll discuss that with my son. Sounds good, Rose. Let’s also schedule that follow-up in a month. Yes, please! I’ll handle that, and I’ll confirm via email. Thank you, Margaret, I appreciate your help! Of course, Rose! Take care, and we’ll talk soon. You too, bye! Bye!
